summary: ORBIT is an interactive astronaut health-monitoring and decision-support prototype designed for long-duration space missions. It brings health indicators, guided self-assessments, personalized daily routines, and accessible health information into a unified interface. Through an astronaut-centered dashboard and Pip, an interactive mission companion, ORBIT explores how crews could monitor their well-being, recognize changes over time, and take informed action with reduced dependence on immediate ground support.
details:
Long-duration spaceflight presents a critical challenge: astronauts must maintain their physical and psychological health while operating in isolated environments where communication delays can limit immediate medical support. ORBIT addresses this challenge by transforming fragmented health observations into an integrated, accessible, and actionable astronaut wellness experience. ORBIT is an interactive health-monitoring and decision-support prototype that unifies daily health check-ins, longitudinal observations, mission scheduling, and personalized wellness activities within a single platform.

ORBIT follows a four-stage workflow: Record → Compare → Queue → Follow Up. Astronauts record observations, compare them against historical trends, identify changes requiring attention, and organize follow-up activities. For example, a six-hour sleep report compared with an eight-hour historical average can prompt an illustrative review and scheduled follow-up. The platform also integrates nutrition, movement, recovery, and psychological well-being into everyday mission routines. Pip, ORBIT's interactive mission companion, provides contextual guidance and encourages engagement with health-monitoring activities.

ORBIT's innovation lies in connecting health information with actionable mission routines rather than presenting isolated measurements. Its human-centered design emphasizes accessibility, reduced cognitive burden, and astronaut autonomy particularly important for missions beyond low Earth orbit. By combining longitudinal monitoring, structured follow-ups, and an engaging gamified, ORBIT explores how future systems could support earlier recognition of health changes, more consistent monitoring, and greater crew independence from ground-based assistance.

This was built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, ORBIT operates as a lightweight, browser-based application. Development incorporated ChatGPT and Codex for AI-assisted programming and design.

The project draws on NASA Human Research Program research concerning the hazards of human spaceflight. Its current implementation uses synthetic astronaut data and illustrative thresholds to demonstrate functional workflows, not clinically validated diagnostics. Future development would involve physiological sensor integration, secure health-data infrastructure, and clinical validation. Our vision is to make astronaut health monitoring not simply informative, but intuitive, integrated, and actionable.
